uncertainties.issue: The comment at product-lifecycle-runtime.ts:182-188 claims the panel's product-delivery composition passes the product-delivery lifecycle, but tracker-view/product-delivery-composition.mjs exports only Delivery providers (no lifecycleDefinition). In production src/ the only lifecycleDefinition assignment is the productBuildLifecycle default; productDeliveryLifecycle is passed only by factory-proof test drivers. Fresh tracker-view starts therefore pin product-build unless a host explicitly passes product-delivery.

release continuation (approval-required -> authorized child) requires a parent whose definition contained the delivery-release stage; with the production default lifecycle being product-build (no delivery-release), the approval-required boundary is only reachable in product-delivery runs. Recorded as a composition-condition consequence, not resolved in code.

Workplace loop-state vocabulary (idle, queued, leased, running, verifying, repair_wait, effect_pending, paused, terminal) is enforced inside ProductionCellNodeExecutor reconcile branches; the authoritative state-transition CAS lives in ProductionCellCoordinator/SqliteWorkplaceRepository which this map cites but does not fully enumerate edge-by-edge.

factory-execution-routes.json declares default executor kind 'claude-cli' with an empty routes table; the runner fails closed on the bare claude CLI (FACTORY_CLAUDE_BACKEND_FORBIDDEN) and resolves the opencode shim via SAGA_REAL_CLAUDE_PATH. The declared default kind name is legacy wording for the shim-backed executor, not an invocation of the retired claude CLI.

Delivery publication/observation in the default panel composition (local-dry-run) fail closed by throwing delivery-provider-not-configured; the local-git-source-tag composition wires a real source-tag provider. Which composition is installed is an environment decision (SAGA_PRODUCT_LIFECYCLE_COMPOSITION), so e47/e48 outcomes depend on the installed provider.

terminal.failed is shared as the lifecycle-level failed status across all stages; the map consolidates it into one terminal node. Stage-specific failure semantics (e.g. discovery failed vs delivery failed) differ in certificate content but not in terminal status value.

development-continuation and development-verification-continuation packages are installed by the CLI bootstrap and their module refs are consumed by the development output resolver, but their ProcessModule flows are continuation-only (reached via operator continue/redevelop); they are represented as continuation nodes rather than expanded stage graphs.
